Strategic objective: Replace development tokens with production Human Account identity and independent Service identities.
Why it is not Release 1: The pilot safely identifies invited users with revocable development tokens.
Trigger to revisit: Before production access or unattended API use.

Capability area: MCP security shim and delegated RBAC
Strategic objective: Propagate trusted identity to vendor MCP servers and enforce platform-specific access at each provider call.
Why it is not Release 1: Release 1 uses development data and MCP servers configured explicitly read-only.
Trigger to revisit: Before sensitive or production provider data is exposed.

Strategic objective: Move Integration configuration from reviewed JSON to normalized, immutable PostgreSQL publications.
Why it is not Release 1: The existing JSON snapshot is sufficient for a controlled pilot.
Trigger to revisit: When Integration changes make reviewed JSON a delivery bottleneck.

Strategic objective: Support Private, Public and restricted Skill lifecycles with governed validation and publication.
Why it is not Release 1: Git already supplies review and publication for the fixed Public catalogue.
Trigger to revisit: When Private authoring or catalogue scale becomes a validated need.

Strategic objective: Provide a separate application for visualising, validating and publishing Integration definitions.
Why it is not Release 1: Authoring is not required to demonstrate runtime value.
Trigger to revisit: After the strategic Integration publication model is stable.

Strategic objective: Add explicit cancellation and new-topic transitions without allowing incomplete Goals to resume.
Why it is not Release 1: The pilot uses one active request and the existing clarification behaviour.
Trigger to revisit: When pilot usage establishes the required Goal transition behaviour.

Strategic objective: Add retention, deletion, administration and production request limits based on pilot usage.
Why it is not Release 1: Advanced lifecycle controls are not required for the invited pilot.
Trigger to revisit: When pilot usage establishes retention and request-control requirements.

Strategic objective: Assess ADA and GCP telemetry before adding any MOSAIC-specific usage ledger.
Why it is not Release 1: Chargeback is not needed to validate the product and ADA/GCP coverage is not yet known.
Trigger to revisit: After production identity and telemetry are stable.
